title: Brazil's President Says 'No Way!' to New U.S. Tariffs
summary: Imagine you made a new friend, but then they suddenly said you had to pay extra to share your snacks. That's how Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva feels about the United States right now. On Tuesday, the U.S. announced a 25% tariff—a tax on imported goods—on certain products from Brazil. Lula said he was surprised and 'could not accept the treatment' his country received. Just last month, Lula met with President Trump at the White House and left feeling hopeful that relations were improving. The two leaders had clashed before over trade and politics. Trump has been friendly with Brazil's former far-right president, Jair Bolsonaro, who is now in prison for trying to overturn an election. The U.S. says the new tariffs are because of unfair trade practices, like illegal deforestation and limited access to Brazil's ethanol market. But experts point out that the U.S. actually sells more to Brazil than it buys—a trade surplus, not a deficit. Lula said Brazil still wants to work with the U.S., but will look for other trading partners if needed. The tariffs won't start right away; there's a public comment period until July. Some important products like beef, coffee, and aircraft parts are not included. Still, this feels like a step backward for two countries that were just starting to get along.
why_it_matters: Tariffs can make everyday products more expensive for families and can strain friendships between countries, affecting everything from jobs to the environment.

background_read: Brazil is the largest country in South America and a major exporter of beef, coffee, and other products. The U.S. and Brazil have had both friendly and tense moments over trade. President Lula (who was elected in 2022) had just met with President Trump to improve ties when the tariff announcement surprised him. Tariffs are often used in trade disputes, but they can raise prices for everyday people.
Article_Structure: WHO: Brazil's President Lula da Silva and U.S. President Trump.
WHAT: The U.S. announced a 25% tariff on certain Brazilian imports, surprising Brazil.
WHERE: The dispute is between the United States and Brazil.
WHY: The U.S. cites unfair trade practices like deforestation and ethanol market limits, though experts note the U.S. actually has a trade surplus with Brazil.

perspectives.description: Some American workers and companies feel tariffs protect their jobs from cheaper foreign goods and punish unfair practices.
Brazilian farmers and exporters say the tariffs are unfair and could hurt their livelihoods without solving the real issues.
Economists worry that trade fights can lead to higher prices for everyone and damage the environment if countries stop cooperating.
